description_en: Jeju's biggest and longest-running permanent market, a covered maze of stalls selling seafood, tangerines, local snacks and souvenirs just a few minutes from the old city centre. In the evening a street-food night market sets up inside the market (enter around Gate 8).
opening_hours: Market approx. 07:00-21:00 (average; varies by stall). Night market: Nov-Apr 18:00-24:00, May-Oct 19:00-24:00 (stalls close early when sold out)
closed_days: none (open year-round including holidays; individual stalls vary)
admission_note: Free entry; pay per item. Public parking: first 30 min free, then paid.
terrain: flat paved alleys under a covered arcade; very crowded in the evening and at weekends
notes: Hours conflict: VisitJeju KR (updated 2026-11-11) gives market 07:00-21:00 and seasonal night-market hours; KTO data (ktriptips mirror) and older listings give 08:00-21:00 and night market 18:00-24:00 year-round. Used VisitJeju. Night market currently (Nov) 18:00 start. Jibun differs: VisitJeju lists 이도일동 1436-7 vs source data 일도일동 1491-1; road address 관덕로14길 20 is consistent across VisitJeju and KTO. English VisitJeju lists the customer support centre at 14 Gwandeok-ro. Restroom 'available' per KTO-derived listing; a visitor blog says restrooms are in the public parking building (elevator to ground floor). No official wheelchair/accessible-restroom data found; a parenting site says strollers can get through but aisles get very crowded. official_url is the VisitJeju (Jeju Tourism Organization) page; no standalone market website confirmed. avg_stay is an estimate.

description_en: A wooded volcanic hill (about 148 m) beside Jeju Port, turned into a city park with pine-shaded paths, exercise areas, a pavilion and the Mochungsa memorial grounds. Its summit is a classic spot for watching the sun set over the harbour and city.
image_source: VISITJEJU (제주관광공사) official photo - licence terms not stated
terrain: uphill paved and dirt paths through pine forest, with stone staircases (e.g. to the Mochungsa memorial tower)
notes: Address/phone conflict: VisitJeju (updated 2026-11-11) = 사라봉동길 74 (건입동), 064-728-3605; KTO data (ktriptips mirror, updated 2026-11-11) = 사라봉길 75 (건입동), 064-728-4643. Used VisitJeju. English name: VisitJeju 'Sarabong Park', KTO 'Sarabong Peak'. Height cited as 148 m in most sources, 143 m in one. Accessibility: VisitJeju barrier-free fields list '단차없음' (no level change) but rate assistance need as '아주 어려움' (very difficult) - conflicting, so wheelchair_ok set false based on the overall rating. has_stairs based on VisitJeju photos showing stone stairways in the park. has_seating based on KTO listing of an octagonal pavilion (팔각정) and exercise facilities. Restroom 'available' per KTO. Image licence on VisitJeju is not published; a Commons alternative is only a nearby road photo (File:Sarabong-gil, Jeju-si, Jeju-do, South Korea - panoramio.jpg, CC BY 3.0). avg_stay is an estimate (one visitor review suggests ~1 hour walk). Category could also be oreum_hike.

description_en: A small 67 m volcanic cone right next to Jeju International Airport, reached by a short but steep path from Doduhang port. The grassy summit gives open views of the sea, the city and landing planes, plus the popular tree-framed 'Kisses Zone' photo spot.
opening_hours: 24h / always open (no set hours; access can occasionally be restricted)
admission_note: Free; parking available near trailhead (fee not confirmed)
terrain: short steep climb on earth/timber step trails under trees; open grassy summit
notes: No dedicated phone; VisitJeju/KTO refer visitors to the Jeju Tourist Information Center 064-740-6000. Jibun conflict: VisitJeju 도두일동 산 2, VisitJeju EN 산 1, source data 산 3-2; road address 도두항길 4-17 (trailhead) consistent in VisitJeju and KTO. Height 67 m per Wikipedia. VisitJeju lists convenience facilities 화장실 and 유도 및 안내시설, no barrier-free facilities, and rates assistance need '아주 어려움' (very difficult) -> wheelchair_ok false. KTO lists separate men/women restrooms at Dodubong Park. has_stairs based on Commons photo File:Dodubong_09.jpg showing a stepped trail. Summit seating not confirmed. Climb time and avg_stay are estimates; fatigue 2 because the climb is short despite being an oreum. Pets on leash allowed per VisitJeju. Night-time visits possible but trail lighting not confirmed.

description_en: The closest swimming beach to downtown Jeju and the airport, known for its grey-sand shore and the pair of red and white horse-shaped lighthouses on the breakwater. A pine grove with a campsite sits behind the sand, and it is a favourite spot for sunsets.
opening_hours: 24h / always open (beach area). Swimming only in the official season: 2026 season was Jun 24 - Sep 6, 10:00-19:00, with night swimming Jul 15 - Aug 15 until 21:00
terrain: flat sand beach; wooden boardwalk and paved paths through the pine grove; walk along the breakwater to the lighthouses
notes: Name: VisitJeju title '이호테우해수욕장'; KTO uses '이호테우해변'. Jibun conflict: VisitJeju 이호2동 1600-1 vs source data 이호일동 1599-1. 2026 season dates (Jun 24 - Sep 6) and hours (10:00-19:00, night to 21:00 Jul 15 - Aug 15) come from news/blog summaries, not an official notice I could open; VisitJeju EN text is older ('open through end of August, night 19:00-21:00'). Out of season (now, November) there is no lifeguard swimming. Accessibility: in summer 2026 Jeju City ran Iho Tewoo as a pilot 'barrier-free beach' with 2 free amphibious wheelchairs and life jackets, and reported a short, well-kept route from the parking lot to the sand; the pilot ended Sep 6, 2026 and continuation is undecided -> wheelchair_ok 'partial'. No source on accessible restrooms/showers (article notes showering is hard for wheelchair users). Restroom and public parking per VisitJeju convenience list; seating based on VisitJeju mention of a viewing rest area (전망휴게소) plus pavilion/boardwalk seen in Commons photos. avg_stay is an estimate.

description_en: A free, city-run arboretum on the slopes of Gwangi Oreum in Jeju City, with themed gardens of native and subtropical plants, a bamboo grove and a forest-bathing area. Paved walking loops make it an easy green escape, and the outdoor paths stay open into the evening.
opening_hours: Outdoor gardens & paths: open year-round (official site says walkable until 23:00). Indoor halls: 09:00-18:00 (Mar-Nov), 09:00-17:00 (Dec-Feb)
closed_days: Outdoor: none. Indoor halls closed on Seollal and Chuseok (the day itself)
admission_note: Free admission. Paid parking (car: 1,000 KRW first 2 h; 10 min free) during 09:00-18:00 (Mar-Nov) / 09:00-17:00 (Dec-Feb)
image_source: VISITJEJU (제주관광공사) official photo - licence terms not stated
terrain: paved and gravel garden paths on a gentle hillside; steeper forest-bath trail up the oreum slope
notes: Hours from the official arboretum site; it says outdoor areas are 'always open' and also 'walkable until 23:00' - treat as open until 23:00 in practice. VisitJeju EN wrongly lists winter hours as 09:00-18:00; official = 09:00-17:00 Dec-Feb. Accessibility from VisitJeju barrier-free fields (updated 2026-11-11): independent access possible, no level changes, low-floor bus access, accessible restroom, elevator, accessible parking, manual wheelchair rental; assistance need rated '쉬움' (easy). Caveat: the forest-bathing trail climbs Gwangi Oreum and was not checked for steps, so has_stairs left null. Seating: official site lists 3 pergolas and a multipurpose rest area. Picnic food only in the designated area below the parking lot; no pets. Commons alternative image: File:Arboretum_of_Halla1.jpg (User:Mar del Este, CC BY 3.0, night shot). avg_stay is an estimate (VisitJeju story says it takes more than an hour to explore).
